Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Raheem

Surah al-Inshiqaq

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿When the sky is split open﴾

The discussion of this has already preceded at the beginning of Surah al-Infitar, at His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When the sky is cleaved asunder﴾ [al-Infitar: 1], and the reference is to the words of our Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) in the two surahs ash-Shura and Qaf.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 84, verse 2:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And it hearkens to its Lord and it is right that it should⦆ [Qur'an 84:2]

The root meaning of "adhina" (أذِنَ, to hearken, to give ear) has already been explained in surah al-Jumu'ah, when discussing the adhan (the call to prayer). "Wa-adhinat" here means it listened and obeyed. "Wa-huqqat" means that it is entitled (haqqa lahā) or that it is deserving of this, i.e., there is no obstacle preventing this command.

Some exegetes have understood "adhinat" in a figurative sense: since there was no resistance on its part to being split open, this was equivalent to compliance and hearkening.

We have already noted that the inanimate things, in relation to God the Exalted, have a state that is not like their state in relation to created beings, in the first discussion of "al-Hashr" concerning the meaning of the glorification (tasbih) of inanimate things.

This has come explicitly with regard to the heavens and the earth. Among that is the saying of God the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72], and the saying of God the Exalted: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: "Come willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly."﴾ [Fussilat: 11].

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾

That is: it is leveled and its mountains are removed, and its valleys are leveled, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they ask you about the mountains. Say, "My Lord will blow them away with a blast."﴾ ﴿And He will leave it as a level plain, in which you will see no crookedness or elevation.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 105-107].

From this is the report from Ibn 'Abbas and from 'Ali. Ibn Kathir related this second one from Ibn Jarir, with its chain, to 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will stretch the earth like a hide, until no person among mankind will have anything but the place of his two feet, and I will be the first to be called." The hadith [continues].

And from Ibn 'Abbas: it will be stretched as a tanned hide ('ukaziyy) is stretched. And in al-Qurtubi, from Ibn 'Abbas: "It will be increased by such-and-such."

Al-Razi said: it means the earth is replaced by another earth. The reality is that the replacement of the earth with another earth does not mean that this existing one is taken away and a new earth brought, because of what came in the hadith of the adhan: "There is no stone, clod, or tree that hears the voice of the muezzin but it will bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection." What is brought anew cannot bear witness to something it did not witness. In any case, the moving of the mountains and the leveling of the earth undoubtedly produces an increase in the surface of the earth and its extent. So whether it is stretched by such-and-such, as Ibn 'Abbas said, or stretched by widening its hide and increasing its expanse, after it casts out what is in its belly like a thick object when pressed, so that its thickness lightens and its extent grows, as His saying the Exalted indicates: ﴿No! When the earth is pounded to powder, pounded and crushed﴾ [Al-Fajr: 21].

And His saying: ﴿And when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast, and the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with one blow, then on that Day the Great Event will occur, and the sky will be split open, for it will be frail that Day﴾ [Al-Haqqah: 13-16].

So the stretching of the earth is due to its being crushed, and so its expanse is increased. Perhaps this is the aspect to which the Qur'an bears witness, combining both matters here: ﴿and the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with one blow, then on that Day the Great Event will occur, and the sky is split open﴾. This accords with what is in this surah: ﴿When the sky is split open﴾, and after it: ﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾.

And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 84, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it casts out what is within it and empties itself﴾ (p-468). It has been said: "It casts out its treasures and empties itself of them." This was refuted on the grounds that this may occur before the Hour.

And it has been said: "It casts out" the dead, "and empties itself" of them after they have risen and been resurrected from their graves; so no one remains within the belly of the earth.

His saying, may He be exalted: "and empties itself," meaning: after it had been for them a container (kifat), for the living and the dead, and after it had been for them a cradle (mihad), it expels them and empties itself of them. This increases the terror of the situation, its severity, and the constriction upon the servants, and that they have no refuge and no escape except to Allah, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿No! There is no refuge﴾ ﴿To your Lord on that Day is the place of rest﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 11-12].

Allah's saying: ﴿And it listens to its Lord and is obligated [to do so]﴾

That is: just as the sky listens [to its Lord], the whole of creation is an obedient ear, submitting to the commands of Allah, willingly or unwillingly.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 84, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, indeed you are labouring toward your Lord with arduous labour, and you will meet Him﴾.

It has been said: "al-insan" (mankind) is used generically (li-l-jins), and it has also been said that it refers to a single individual, namely Muhammad (ﷺ). But the context indicates the first meaning, because of the division that follows: "As for he who is given his record in his right hand" and "As for he who is given his record in his left hand," for this cannot apply to a single individual but only to the species as a whole. On the basis that it is generic, "kadh" (kadh, arduous labour) means work that exhausts the self.

Ibn Muqbil said:

"And the age is but two spells: in one of them I die, and in the other I strive (abtaghi) for life, labouring (akdah)."

Another poet said, indicating that kadh carries the sense of fatigue (nasab):

"The brightness of every good life has passed away, and I remain labouring (akdahu) for life and toiling (anṣabu)."

This is supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed We have created man in toil﴾ [al-Balad: 4], as we have mentioned in its place.

A note.

From this noble Qur'anic presentation, beginning with the transformation of the states of the cosmos, heaven and earth, and the placing of man within it laboring toward his Lord ﴿with arduous labour, and you will meet Him﴾, that is: with his knowledge which he acquires through his labour. For the wise, discerning person does not direct his labour except toward what pleases God and what he himself is pleased with. And when he meets his Lord, as long as he is labouring, there is no doubt of it, as is observed.

Another note.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind﴾ is general in its inclusion of every human being, whatever his condition, whether believer or disbeliever, righteous or wicked, and all of them labour and strive diligently to attain what they are bound toward. As in the hadith: "Act, for each is made easy for that for which he was created," meaning: and striving in it and content with it. This is the ultimate of the wisdom of the All-Knowing, the All-Aware.

What is also worthy of mention is that if the heaven, with the greatness of its body, and the earth, with the extent of its foundation, ﴿hearkened to its Lord and was obligated﴾, though they did not bear a trust and will not be questioned about any duty, then how about man in his weakness?! ﴿Are you more difficult to create or is the heaven?﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 27]. Yet he has borne the trust of responsibility (taklif), whereas they feared it, and man bore it. He was therefore more worthy of hearing and obeying in his labour, until he meets his Lord with that which pleases Him.

﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand﴾, ﴿he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning﴾, ﴿and he will return to his family joyful﴾. ﴿But as for him who is given his record behind his back﴾, ﴿he will call for destruction﴾, ﴿and he will burn in a Blaze﴾. ﴿Indeed, he was among his family, joyful﴾. ﴿Indeed, he thought he would never return﴾.

In this detail there is an explanation of the destiny of man as a result of his toil, and of what was recorded against him in the book of his deeds. This comes after the verse in "al-Infitar" where He said: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do. Indeed, the righteous will be in pleasure, and indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire﴾ [al-Infitar: 10–14].

In "al-Mutaffifin" it came: ﴿No! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 7], then after it: ﴿No! Indeed, the record of the righteous is in Illiyyin﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 18].

The mention here of how they are given these records indicates the interconnection of these surahs with one another, in explaining the end of the whole world and the destiny of man as a result of his deeds.

The Shaykh has previously discussed the matter of receiving the records in the right hand, the left hand, and from behind the back, at the words of His Exalted saying: ﴿The Day We will call every people with their leader﴾ in the surah "al-Isra'" up to His saying: ﴿So whoever is given his record in his right hand﴾ [al-Isra': 71]. He also explained the conditions of the two groups, the People of the Right and the People of the Left, and referred back to the beginning of that surah.

And His saying: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it﴾ [al-Kahf: 49], in the surah "al-Kahf". Here, He, glorified and exalted, mentioned one state from the states of both groups.

As for the first: ﴿he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning﴾, which is merely the presentation (of deeds) without debate, as in the hadith of ʿAishah, may Allah be pleased with her: "Whoever is subjected to debate in his reckoning will be punished."

As for the second: he calls upon destruction (thubur) against himself, and thubur is ruin. From it comes the word muwāṭaʾah ("agreeing upon something"), which is called muthābarah (persistence), because he is as though he wants to destroy himself in his pursuit of it.

Here there is a remarkable contrast of great importance, between two joys, one of which is deferred and the other immediate.

As for the first, concerning him who is given his record in his right hand, he returns to his family joyful, calling out in happiness: ﴿Here, read my record!﴾ [al-Haqqah: 19]. His family at that time are in Paradise, among the houris and the youths, and among his relatives who entered Paradise, as in His saying: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence, which they will enter, along with whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants﴾ [al-Ra'd: 23].

And His saying: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith – We will join them with their descendants﴾ [al-Tur: 21]. Although they are joined to them, they are (still) of their family. This is part of the completion of the blessing, that he informs those among his family whom he knows (of it). This increases the servant's joy, and it is the lasting joy.

The other is an immediate joy, and it belongs to those who are given their records in their left hands, because they were joyful in their hopes in the world. How vast is the difference between one joy and another!

Here He has explained the result of their joy in the world: that they will burn in a Blaze. He did not explain the cause of the joy of the others here, but He explained it in another place, which is their fear of Allah, in His saying: ﴿They said, "Indeed, we were before, among our families, fearful. So Allah conferred favor upon us and protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind. Indeed, we used to call upon Him. Indeed, He is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful"﴾ [al-Tur: 26–28].

It is said here that Allah, glorified is He, does not combine two fears upon His servant, nor does He give him two securities together. Whoever fears Him in this world, He grants him security in the Hereafter: ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens﴾ [al-Rahman: 46].

﴿But as for he who feared the standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from desire, indeed, Paradise will be his refuge﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 40–41].

As for whoever felt secure from the plan of Allah, fulfilled all his desires, and did not care, he will be given his record in his left hand and will burn in a Blaze, as in His saying: ﴿And the companions of the left – what are the companions of the left? – In scorching wind and boiling water, and in the shade of black smoke, neither cool nor pleasant. Indeed, they were before that given to luxury, and they used to persist in the great violation, and they used to say, "When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected?"﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 41–47], denying the Resurrection.

His saying, "Indeed, he thought he would never return," is the very same thought mentioned in these verses: ﴿Indeed, he thought he would never return﴾.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, he thought he would never return﴾ – this thinking is like what came earlier concerning the defrauders: ﴿Do they not think that they will be resurrected for a tremendous Day?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 4–5]. This suggests that the lack of faith in the Resurrection, or doubt about it, is the driver of every evil and the destroyer of every good, and that faith in the Last Day is the starting point of every good and the preventer of every evil. Faith in the Resurrection is the starting point of all righteous deeds, as at the beginning of the Mushaf: ﴿Guidance for the righteous﴾ [al-Baqarah: 2].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 84, verse 10:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

Surah al-Inshiqaq

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But as for him who is given his record behind his back﴾ — the verse.

This noble verse indicates that whoever is not given his record in his right hand, he is given it behind his back. Yet there is another verse from which it is understood that he is given it in his left hand, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, "Oh, I wish I had not been given my record"﴾ [al-Haqqah: 25] — the verse.

The answer is evident: there is no contradiction between his taking it in his left hand and his being given it behind his back, because the disbeliever's right hand is chained to his neck, and his left hand is placed behind his back, so he takes his record with it.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 84, verse 16:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So I swear by the twilight﴾ ﴿and by the night and what it gathers﴾ ﴿and by the moon when it becomes full﴾ ﴿you will surely travel from state to state.﴾

Ash-shafaq (twilight) linguistically means the thinness of a thing.

Al-Qurtubi said: It is said "shay'un shafiq," meaning a thing with no cohesion because of its thinness. "Ashfaqa 'alayhi" means his heart became tender toward him. Ash-shafaqah, the noun from al-ishfaq, is tenderness of heart, and likewise ash-shafaq.

The poet said:

*They love my life, and I love its death out of tenderness,*
*and death is the most honourable guest to alight upon the sacred precinct.*

So ash-shafaq is the remainder of the sun's light and its redness, as if that tenderness comes from the sunlight.

It is related from al-Khalil: Ash-shafaq is the redness from the sunset until the time of the late ('ishaʾ) prayer when it departs. It is said: "ghaba ash-shafaq" (the twilight has set). End of quotation.

[p. 472] This is what the three imams hold in determining the time of the maghrib prayer: from the sunset until the disappearance of ash-shafaq, which is the redness after sunset, as al-Khalil said.

According to Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, ash-shafaq is the whiteness that follows it.

The Shaykh (may God's mercy be upon us and upon him) had earlier, in explaining the times of the five prayers at His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So glorify God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ ﴿and to Him is praise in the heavens and the earth, and in the late afternoon and when you reach noon﴾ [al-Rum: 17–18], given his preference that ash-shafaq is the redness.

Al-Qurtubi relayed an opinion, saying: The philosophers claimed that the whiteness never sets at all.

Al-Khalil said: I climbed the lighthouse of Alexandria and gazed at the whiteness, and I saw it moving from horizon to horizon, and I did not see it set.

Ibn Uways said: I saw it extend until the rising of dawn. Then he said: Our scholars said: since its time does not renew itself, its consideration is dropped. End of quotation.

Thus, by this, he favours the view of the majority regarding the meaning of ash-shafaq. The texts on this from the Sunnah have some discussion. Al-Daraqutni related a marfu' hadith (a hadith traced back to the Prophet ﷺ): "Ash-shafaq is the redness."

Al-Shawkani discussed it, then mentioned those who hold this view from the Companions: Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, and 'Ubadah. From the imams: al-Shafi'i, Ibn Abi Layla, al-Thawri, and Abu Yusuf and Muhammad among the jurists, and al-Khalil and al-Farra' among the linguists.

You see that Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, who were companions of Abu Hanifa, agreed with the majority.

Also in Sharh al-Hidayah there is a narration from Abu Hanifa.

As for what al-Qurtubi mentioned, it is open to scrutiny, namely regarding the non-disappearance of the whiteness. The known view among astronomers is that between the red and the white there is a difference of two degrees, and a degree equals four minutes, so the difference is slight. And God knows best.

His saying: ﴿and by the night and what it gathers﴾ means gathering and collecting a large amount of something. From this the wasq (a fixed measure of grain, sixty ṣāʿ) is named. It is said that there are other meanings for it, but this is the most preferred.

The meaning here: and by the night and what it gathers of created things. It is said: it is as if He swore by everything, like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So I swear by what you see﴾ ﴿and what you do not see﴾ [al-Haqqah: 38–39].

His saying: ﴿and by the moon when it becomes full﴾, that is, when it expands, i.e., when its light is complete. It is the form ifta'ala (the eighth verbal form) from wasaqa. The morphological rule is that the first radical of the mithal verb (the verb whose first radical is waw) when formed on the ifta'ala pattern, the waw is changed into ta' and the ta' is assimilated into the ta' of the form, as in: "wasaltuhu fa-ittasala" (I connected it, so it connected), and "wazantuhu fa-ittazana" (I weighed it, so it weighed); here likewise "awtasaqa" (it became full).

His saying: ﴿you will surely travel from state to state﴾

Ibn Jarir said: The reciters differed in its recitation. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Mas'ud and his companions, Ibn 'Abbas, and most of the reciters of Makkah and Kufa read "latarkabanna" with a fatha on the ta' and the ba'. The reciters of this differed in its meaning. Some said: it means, O Muhammad, and it means the states of ascent, elevation, and hardships with the people. This meaning is related from Mujahid and Ibn 'Abbas.

It was also said: "ṭabaqan 'an ṭabaq" means heaven after heaven, i.e., the layers of the heaven. This is related from al-Hasan, Abu al-'Aliyah, and Masruq.

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud that it refers to the heaven whose states change: it splits with clouds, then reddens like molten metal, and so on. He preferred the first recitation and the first meaning.

Most of the reciters of Madinah and some of the Kufans read "latarkubunna" with a ta' and a damma on the ba', in the form of address to all people.

The exegetes mentioned for its meaning, state after state, many meanings: childhood, youth, old age; poverty and wealth; strength and weakness; life, death, and resurrection; ease and hardship; to everything the word can bear.

Al-Qurtubi said: All of them are possible, and all of them are intended. What appears to me, and God knows best, is that this refers to people in general and will happen on the Day of Resurrection, since the context concerns the fundamentals of resurrection: ﴿When the sky splits open﴾, ﴿and when the earth is stretched out﴾, ﴿As for he who is given his record in his right hand﴾, and he mentioned the reckoning that turns over. Then the expression in the future tense, "latarkabanna" (you will surely travel). If it were about worldly affairs, such as changes of conditions, the present or past tense would have been more appropriate for it. And even if it is future, what will come in time, it is not new, since the changing of conditions in the matter of life is a settled matter in minds and does not need this style.

As for the affairs of the Hereafter, of resurrection, gathering, presentation, the scale, the bridge, the flying of records, and the differing states of people according to the differing stations in the plains of the Resurrection, these are the most fitting to be warned about and cautioned against, and to act for, in one's toil toward one's Lord. Therefore this was brought, and it implies the continuation of the human state after the toil into multiple states and differing degrees.

And if we consider the state of what was sworn by, in terms of the development of its condition: from twilight, or the last light of the sun; then night, and what it gathers and covers with its darkness; then the moon, which begins as a crescent until its light is complete. It would be a transition from the changing movements of time to the changing states of the human being with certainty, and that the One who is able to do this in this world is able to do it in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 84, verse 25:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward uninterrupted.﴾

It has been said: al-mann (المَنّ) means cutting off and diminishing. From it is the saying of the poet:

Over a slain wild ram (qahd), whose carcass is scattered, are predatory birds (ghabs), whose prey is never diminished (ma yumannu ta'amuha).

The qahd is a kind of sheep with a small reddish tint, its ears small. The kawasib are the wild beasts, that is, wolves or predators whose prey is never cut off.

Al-Qurtubi said: "I cut the rope (mannantu al-habl)" when you cut it.

Nafi' ibn al-Azraq asked Ibn 'Abbas about it, and he said: "Not cut off." He said: "Does the Arabic language know this?" He said: "Yes, the brother of Yashkur has known it, where he says:"

Then you see behind them, from the speed of the running, a mannin (dust-cloud), as if it were scattered particles (ahba').

Al-Mubarrad said: al-manin is dust, because they cut it off behind them.

It has also been said: "ghayr mamnun" means not bestowed upon them as a favour, so that the blessing may be complete for them.

Ibn Jarir said: "ghayr mamnun" means not counted (ghayr mahsub) and not diminished. He reported this from Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid.

Ibn Kathir said: "not cut off," like His saying: ﴿a gift not cut off﴾ [Hud: 108]. He rejected the view of those who say it means "not bestowed as a favour upon them," because Allah may bestow favour upon His servants, and they did not enter Paradise except by Allah's grace and bounty upon them. End of quotation.

What supports Ibn Jarir's view, "not counted," is the general statement of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account﴾ [Al 'Imran: 37], and the specific statement of His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer—those will enter Paradise, being provided for therein without account﴾ [Ghafir: 40].

And His saying: ﴿a reward from your Lord, a sufficient gift﴾ [al-Naba': 36]; here "hisaban" means "kafiyan" (sufficient), from your saying "hasbi," meaning "kafini" (suffices me).

What appears—and Allah knows best—is that each of the two meanings is intended, and there is no barrier to this. What Ibn Kathir held does not conflict with the view of the others, because the forbidden mann is that which contains harm and diminishment, as in His saying: ﴿then they do not follow what they spent with reminder (mann) or injury﴾ [al-Baqarah: 262]. As for the mann of Allah upon His servant, it is itself honour and nearness to Him, glory be to Him. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.
